proposedFirstIteration.property: Pure referral create and patch types no longer require a type-only dependency on the effectful server store, while all existing store import paths and runtime behavior remain compatible.
explicitlyExcluded: Moving local-file or PostgreSQL adapter code
Changing SQL, transactions, locks, retries, audit events, authorization, validation, normalization, duplicate review, workflow, or assessment synchronization
Changing browser component imports in the same iteration
Adding a new abstraction, module, dependency, feature flag, migration, or compatibility implementation

files.dependencyDirection: Server-only persistence boundary may depend on stable referral types, pure policy, database/persistence adapters, and workflow policy; routes and server services may depend on its public store API. Browser modules must not gain runtime imports from it.
files.observedPurpose: Selects the durable adapter and currently owns public store contracts, local-file persistence, PostgreSQL queries and transactions, normalization, mapping, filtering, audit construction, duplicate review, trash/restore, and referral-coupled work-item and assessment effects.
observedCallers: Referral, trash, file, search, activity, assessment, workflow, operations, calendar, health, and internal reconciliation routes/services
sideEffects: Local JSON file read, atomic replace, chmod, and process-global state
Dynamic assessment-store reads and writes in local mode
Aggregate console warning on local load failure
files.observedFailureBehavior: Returns typed conflicts/blockers/null for expected state outcomes; throws for duplicate packet, suspected duplicate, capacity, invalid cursor, reassignment race, pagination safety limit, database errors, and local persistence errors. PostgreSQL rolls back coupled transaction effects; local reassignment and persistence are not fully atomic.

staticPrompts.prompt: Large module (3036 lines): split by behavior before adding more responsibilities.
staticPrompts.evidence: The module contains separately characterizable contracts, adapter selection, two adapters, queries, mappings, mutation policy, audit construction, projections, and cross-store synchronization.

staticPrompts.prompt: Contains runtime console logging; verify messages cannot include PHI, tokens, query strings, or upstream bodies.
staticPrompts.evidence: The observed local-load warning contains only fixed service and event names and does not interpolate the error or referral data.

staticPrompts.prompt: Explicitly suppresses a rejected promise; verify this is genuinely optional and observable.
staticPrompts.evidence: The persistence queue deliberately recovers its prior rejected state before attempting the next serialized write. Whether the preceding failed write needs additional operator-visible state is not yet characterized.
staticPrompts.followUp: Owner must decide whether aggregate logging/readiness is required for local persistence recovery before adapter movement.

files.proposedDecisionReason: Split only by independently evidenced responsibility. The first proposed iteration moves two pure mutation types to the existing type owner and preserves store re-exports; adapter or transaction movement is explicitly deferred.

files.dependencyDirection: Stable referral data and mutation shapes may depend only on stable domain vocabularies or type-only external contracts; application, policy, persistence, route, and browser layers may depend on them.
files.observedPurpose: Defines canonical referral, ownership, section, workflow projection, requirement, decision, handoff, assessment projection, and referral-file shapes shared across the application.
observedCallers: Referral store, workflow, assessment, operations, calendar, activity, validation, extraction-adjacent domain modules, API routes, and browser components
files.observedFailureBehavior: Type-only module; compile-time incompatibilities fail TypeScript checks. Its type-level workflow and extraction dependencies can create comprehension or dependency-cycle risk without runtime effects.
files.proposedDecisionReason: Reuse the existing stable type owner for the two pure mutation shapes. Do not turn this file into a universal infrastructure contract or change its workflow/extraction dependency direction without separate owner validation.

files.dependencyDirection: Pure public-input validation may depend on canonical referral types and bounded vocabulary constants; it must not depend on storage, database, route, browser, or external-service implementations.
files.observedPurpose: Validates referral create and public patch payloads, including server-owned fields, text limits, enum values, hashes, document sizes, packet projections, work items, decision projections, and timestamps.
files.observedFailureBehavior: Returns a bounded validation failure with a public message and status, normally 400, before the route invokes persistence.
files.proposedDecisionReason: Keep the validator as the public trust boundary but change its type-only `ReferralPatch` dependency from the effectful store to the stable referral type owner.

files.dependencyDirection: Pure optimistic-section policy may depend on referral field and section types; routes, collaboration UI, workflow, and stores may depend on it.
files.observedPurpose: Maps mutable referral fields to six optimistic-concurrency sections and owns section-version defaults, normalization, incrementing, patch classification, and section-name validation.
files.observedFailureBehavior: Malformed or missing section-version input normalizes to defaults; unsupported patch keys do not claim a section; callers own conflict response behavior.
files.proposedDecisionReason: The file already has one cohesive pure responsibility. It should remain unchanged in the first proposed iteration.
